source_constants.value: TOUCH_RADIUS = 145.0 canvas pixels; ARC_REQUIRED = 1.05 × TAU; DISTANCE_REQUIRED = 400.0 canvas pixels; MOTION_SECONDS_REQUIRED = 1.5 seconds.
Roshan approaches at 360 canvas pixels/second; arrival is within 1.0 pixel. First idle reprompt is after 5.0 seconds; later reprompts after 12.0 seconds, at most three.
The final whole-room sparkle beat waits 0.92 seconds before the completion signal.

timing.assumptions: The code requires about 1.05 circular turns, 400 pixels of in-radius travel and 1.5 seconds of held movement before cleaning. Actual first-time and repeat duration depend on actor start position, route and touch cadence; no child duration is estimated. The 46.463-second probe wall time is not gameplay duration.

tactile.target_size: The scrub accepts a press within a 145-pixel radius of bowl center (290-pixel diameter); it is a circular region, not a measured phone-projected hitbox. Probe code calls it generous, but L04's executed probe did not exercise this controller.
tactile.press_response: A valid begin_gesture claims the finger and resets idle timing. The source does not change grime opacity or brush pose on press alone; grime and brush change after qualifying movement. Headless integration results do not measure the two-frame visual response requirement.
tactile.drag_hold_release: One-finger circular dragging is required. Progress counts only movement while both previous and current points are within the 145-pixel radius; completion requires arc, distance and held-motion thresholds together. Release cancels the owned finger while partial arc/distance/time remain in the controller.
tactile.ownership: Only one finger id is held at a time; a second begin is rejected while _finger is owned. The controller is a full-canvas Control with mouse_filter STOP and receives its GUI input. No physical touch routing or neighboring hit-target competition was tested for the scrub.
tactile.cancellation: Focus loss, pause and teardown cancel the held finger; pause/focus suspension stops approach and hides the pointer. Existing probe_day_one_bathroom_cleanup.gd contains direct assertions for focus/pause cancellation and stale-drag rejection, but those assertions were not part of the executed L04 probe.

play_appeal.hypothesis: Roshan visibly approaching with the brush, followed by a bowl-centered circle cue and grime clearing as the child scrubs, could give a clear cause-and-effect action with a satisfying payoff. Repeated circular motion may feel repetitive if the required arc/distance takes several attempts; replay and child appeal are unmeasured.

evidence: scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_toilet.gd:155-162 (begin_gesture only stores finger, position and idle reset)

observations.reproduction: After Roshan arrives, press inside the bowl radius and hold without moving. The begin handler changes only controller state; grime and brush changes require movement, while the circle/pointer guidance is hidden for the owned-finger state.
observations.child_impact: A child who touches the bowl and pauses may not see that the touch was accepted or understand that a circular drag is now expected. Whether the press itself is sufficiently obvious visually has not been rendered or observed here.
observations.proposed_repair: No repair conclusion without visual/device evidence. Review a press-state acknowledgment that preserves the source art and does not obscure the brush/bowl action.
observations.acceptance_test: At 30 fps on the target phone, press and hold at the bowl center without moving; verify an unambiguous visual response begins within two rendered frames, then verify it transitions coherently into scrub feedback after movement.

observations.title: Touch during Roshan’s approach can be owned before scrubbing is enabled
evidence: scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_toilet.gd:164-167 (move_gesture rejects movement before _arrived but keeps the finger state)
scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_toilet.gd:203-217 (arrival announces while pointer visibility still depends on finger being released)
scripts/probe_day_one_bathroom_cleanup.gd:648-677 (existing controller check presses before arrival, releases, then confirms arrival/pointer; it does not test holding continuously through arrival)
observations.reproduction: Touch inside the bowl radius while Roshan is still approaching and keep holding past arrival. Source allows begin_gesture, rejects pre-arrival drag, and makes pointer visibility false while the finger remains owned. The child-facing impact is a source-based hypothesis, not an executed device observation.
observations.child_impact: A child could start the scrub before the invitation, then see the spoken prompt without the circle/pointer and with no scrub progress until the next movement. That may make the accepted hold feel stuck or unexplained.
observations.proposed_repair: If routed input confirms this ambiguity, either reject/visibly acknowledge early presses and require release/re-touch after arrival, or safely queue the intended gesture with clear visible feedback.
observations.acceptance_test: Drive a routed touch from before approach arrival through arrival; confirm the finger’s ownership, pointer/circle, voice prompt and first scrub motion make the correct next action obvious and cannot strand the input.
